steps.name: Sample QC and count preprocessing
steps.context: Counts: /eval-four-models-v2-without-total-rna-highdup-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 x 13, gene-level Salmon counts). Metadata: /eval-four-models-v2-without-total-rna-highdup-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2: sample, condition). Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. QC caveats from profiling: duplication rate >60% in most libraries (no UMIs), sample_01 ~4x below median library size.
steps.question: Are the 12 samples internally consistent (sample_01 depth outlier, structure of variance between treated and control), and which of the 12000 genes carry enough signal to test for treated-vs-control differences?
steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples + gene-ID column) and metadata.csv (12 samples, 2 columns: sample and condition), verify sample-to-column alignment, compute per-sample library size and detection rate, run PCA/MDS on variance-stabilized counts to check for outliers with special attention to sample_01, and filter lowly expressed genes.
acceptance_criteria: All 12 metadata rows match 12 count columns exactly (1:1, order documented or reordered and verified)
Per-sample table with library size, detected genes, and duplication-rate caveat recorded in the report
PCA/MDS plot of variance-stabilized counts produced; outlier status of sample_01 explicitly stated based on both depth and PCA position
Low-expression filtering applied (genes with CPM > 1 in at least 6 samples, i.e. the size of the smaller group) with the gene count before/after reported
Filtered count matrix and variance-stabilized matrix written as CSV/TSV artifacts

steps.name: Primary differential expression with DESeq2
steps.context: Same files as T1S1. Filtered counts from T1S1. DESeq2 is appropriate because these are raw integer gene counts from Salmon; no UMIs, so no deduplication step is possible and counts are used as delivered.
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control by the primary count-based test, with what effect size and FDR?
steps.description: Fit a DESeq2 model (~condition) on the filtered counts, estimate size factors and dispersions, run the Wald test for treated vs control with Cook's-distance outlier handling, and shrink log2 fold changes with apeglm.
acceptance_criteria: Design matrix is ~condition with treated as the reference-vs-treatment contrast stated explicitly
No observation excluded except through DESeq2's automatic Cook's-distance handling, and every excluded gene reported by name and reason
Full results table (gene, baseMean, log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) for all tested genes written as an artifact, plus a shrunk-LFC table
Independent filtering status and number of genes with padj < 0.05 and padj < 0.1 reported
Note recorded that counts carry no length correction and that the high duplication rate is not correctable post hoc without per-sample duplication metadata

steps.name: Robustness: edgeR QL and sample_01 sensitivity
steps.context: With 6v6, one sample at 4x below median depth, and >60% duplication (unquantifiable post hoc), the primary DESeq2 list must be stress-tested before being reported as the answer. edgeR quasi-likelihood handles small-n dispersion differently; excluding sample_01 tests depth dependence.
steps.question: Do the same genes come out of an independent count-based method and when the low-depth sample is dropped, i.e. which genes are robust to tool and to sample_01?
steps.description: Repeat the treated-vs-control test with edgeR quasi-likelihood (TMM) and with DESeq2 excluding sample_01, then quantify concordance of gene lists across the three analyses.
acceptance_criteria: EdgeR QL fit on the same filtered matrix with TMM normalization, treated-vs-control contrast, same nominal FDR threshold
DESeq2 re-run without sample_01, same design, results saved separately
Concordance table: gene list overlap (FDR < 0.05) across DESeq2-full, DESeq2-no-sample01, and edgeR-QL, with an upset/venn summary and Spearman correlation of test statistics
Each robust gene carries a flag noting in how many of the three analyses it is significant and whether its LFC direction is consistent
Short written assessment of whether the treated-vs-control signal depends on sample_01 or on the choice of tool

steps.name: Consolidated DE results and figures
steps.context: Data volume is small (12000 genes x 12 samples); plots are cheap and needed for QC-verified presentation.
steps.question: What is the final, reviewable answer to 'which genes differ between treated and control', with effect sizes, significance, and a robustness annotation per gene?
steps.description: Merge DESeq2 and edgeR results into one annotated results table with a robustness flag per gene, and produce the volcano, MA, and top-gene heatmap figures.
acceptance_criteria: Final table of significant genes at padj < 0.05 with robustness flag, direction, and shrunk LFC, sorted by padj
Volcano plot of shrunk LFC vs -log10 padj with top genes labelled; MA plot of the primary contrast
Heatmap of top 50 genes by padj across all 12 samples (variance-stabilized, z-scaled)
Explicit statement of how many of the significant genes are called in all three analyses vs only in some

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the DE signal
steps.context: Ranked-list input from T1S2/T1S4. Reference data: the environment stages a human WikiPathways GMT under /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/ (HGNC symbols, '%'-delimited descriptor field). Match GMT symbols to the counts matrix gene identifiers (they are gene-level Salmon IDs); if the IDs are Ensembl or Entrez rather than symbols, map via the human UniProt idmapping file also staged under /mnt/refs (column 19 Ensembl, column 3 Entrez). Do not use the rat or mouse GMTs that are also staged.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are over-represented in the treated-vs-control ranking, giving the gene list functional context?
steps.description: Run fgsea against the WikiPathways Homo sapiens gene sets (HGNC symbols) using the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric, in both directions, to identify pathways enriched among treated-vs-control genes.
acceptance_criteria: GMT parsed from the '%'-delimited descriptor format; pathway size distribution and genes matched per pathway reported
fgsea run on the treated-vs-control Wald-statistic ranking with minSize >= 10; NES, p-value and padj per pathway written as an artifact
Leading-edge genes for the top pathways (padj < 0.25) reported so pathway calls connect back to specific genes from T1S4
If the human GMT is not resolvable at run time, the step reports the gap and exits cleanly rather than substituting a mouse or rat pathway set

plan.title: Treated vs control heart DE with duplication-aware QC
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a small, clean two-group bulk RNA-seq design: 12 heart samples, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, one batch, Salmon gene-level raw counts (12000 genes) from rRNA-depleted, UMI-free total-RNA libraries. The research question is a standard differential-expression question, so the pipeline is the canonical count-based DE workflow: sample-level QC first (the profile flags a >60% duplication rate in most libraries and sample_01 at ~4x below median library size, both of which reduce effective library complexity and inflate noise), low-count filtering, a primary DESeq2 analysis on ~condition with Cook's-distance outlier handling and apeglm LFC shrinkage, then a two-pronged robustness check (edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same counts, and DESeq2 re-run excluding sample_01) because with n=6 per arm plus a low-depth outlier plus high duplication, any single tool's gene list is fragile. Genes are finally consolidated and called robust vs sensitive, and the robust DE signal is mapped to WikiPathways human pathways via fgsea to give the result biological interpretability. No batch correction, surrogate variables, or pairing terms are used: the design is single-batch and unpaired, so the only design factor is condition. Salmon counts are used as delivered (no tximport/length correction is possible from a counts-only matrix); this is standard for gene-level DE but noted as a caveat.
